The test image shows:
- Stem near/at soil level, split open to reveal interior
- White fungal growth on the exterior of the stem base
- Internal vascular discoloration (yellowing/browning)
- Wilted/dead plant with brown collapsed leaves
- Sandy soil context

Key features point to a soilborne stem disease. Top candidates: Southern_Blight (white mycelium at soil line), Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (white cottony growth), Verticillium_Wilt (vascular discoloration). Let me view one reference from each.
Strong match! Southern_Blight reference shows white mycelial growth on the stem base, similar to the test image. Now let me check Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.
Sclerotinia reference shows wilting but no white mycelium at soil line — less similar. Now checking Verticillium_Wilt.
Verticillium_Wilt shows leaf symptoms, no stem base white growth. Now checking Phytophthora_Blight.
Phytophthora_Blight shows dark blackish stem lesions, no white growth. Now checking Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, and Alternaria to complete the 8 required views.
Need one more reference view to complete the required 8. Let me check Late_Blight.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Stem at soil line, split open, showing white fungal growth on exterior stem base, internal yellowing/browning, collapsed dead plant, sandy soil context.
- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_2): White mycelial growth on stem base at soil line — closest match to test image. Same presentation: pulled plant, root system visible, white growth coating stem, sandy soil.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Wilting only, no white stem base growth — less similar.
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Leaf wilting symptoms only — different.
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Dark blackish stem lesions — different.
- **Bacterial_Wilt / Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Diagnostic bacterial streaming tests — different.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Dark canker at stem base, no white growth — less similar.
- **Late_Blight**: Leaf symptoms — different.

The white mycelial growth on the stem base at soil level is the hallmark of Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*), and the reference image matches the test image closely.
